root_idea.summary: The root centers on securing or providing support: a fastening or tie, something used for support, and bodily reliance or reclining.
root_idea.development: The lexical development runs from a cord or means of securing something to making or using a support, then to leaning, resting, and reclining. Related idiomatic extensions include eating while reclining and naming a repast by its association with that posture.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested Form V verb, normalized to its perfect-tense dictionary citation form.
Distinct Quran-attested nominal use, normalized to the singular passive-participial citation form.
Distinct Quran-attested active-participle group, normalized from its plural Quran forms to the singular citation form.

senses.definition: To support oneself or lean upon a staff or other object.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is the first-person imperfect form in the construction “I lean upon it,” referring to a staff.

senses.definition: To lean, rest, or recline upon or against something; to sit in a settled, supported posture.
senses.usage_conditions: The verb may describe resting the back or side against a support or reclining upon a cushion or similar object. The Quranic occurrence has the contextual sense “recline.”
In the Quranic occurrence, the noun denotes food or a repast through its association with reclining during a meal; it is a conventional extension of the reclining-related noun.

senses.definition: One who reclines or sits in a settled, supported posture.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic forms are plural and describe people reclining; the posture is not restricted to leaning on one side and may involve resting against a support.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fastening cord or tie; the means by which something is secured or closed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal lexical branch concerning securing or binding something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lean upon one’s hands or arms.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عَلَى يَدَيْهِ to describe supporting the body on the hands or arms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To provide someone with something upon which to recline, or to prop someone up and make him recline upon a cushion or similar support.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive causative construction involving furnishing or applying a support.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to fall into a reclining posture, including by striking or piercing so that he is thrown onto his side.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or extended causative use describing the result of an assault.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make or provide for oneself something upon which to lean or recline.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported interpretation of the Form VIII entry; the source questions the reading or analysis of this causative-like use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To eat a repast with someone or at someone’s abode.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical or idiomatic use associated with the custom of reclining while eating.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel: to be seized by the pains of labor and cry out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage applied to a camel in labor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A staff or stick used as a support in walking; anything upon which one leans or reclines.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for a physical aid or support.
A personal descriptive use of the noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or object for reclining, such as a chamber, sitting-room, or support used while eating, drinking, or talking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical Arabic nominal use distinct from the Quranic repast sense.

cautions: The Quranic مُتَّكَأٌ in 12:31 is presented under the conventional repast/banquet sense; the related place and reclining-support senses are Classical Arabic meanings, not additional Quranic senses in this packet.
The plural Quranic active-participle forms are represented under the normalized singular headword مُتَّكِئٌ.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The Mufradat entry also records أَوْكَيْتُ السِّقَاءَ and explicitly distinguishes it from أَوْكَأْتُ; because it is presented as a different form, it is not assigned as a direct Quranic Form IV meaning here.

The Mufradat hadith expression يُوكِي بين الصفا والمروة is accompanied by competing interpretations, and no independently supplied QAC location identifies a corresponding Quranic form; it is therefore not assigned as a separate form-level sense.
